strengths: Freshness is not a concern: every scored unit reports snapshot_age_days 0 against max_snapshot_age_days 30, and the swebench-multilingual/multimodal boards report 0 against max_snapshot_age_days 90.

Operational fields are complete and attributed: each route carries input_price, output_price and context_limit with source '~/.pi/agent/models-store.json' and a read_at timestamp one day before reference_time, so no price or limit is asserted without provenance.

The scorecard is conservative about eligibility: run_stage_plan, review_plan and general carry signal 'no_comparable_evidence' rather than a fabricated ranking, and their rows are all eligible false with rank null.
Proxy evidence is explicitly downgraded rather than used: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash's deepswe entry is recorded as 'proxy-family (deliberately not scored)' for publisher 'deepseek-v4-flash'.

Implement's tie handling is transparent and does not overclaim: the rank-1 tie group states 'Capability ranks remain tied' and labels the resolution 'cost-broke-tie', keeping the operational preference separate from capability.

Coverage is reported with missing weight named per capability and never redistributed, so partial rows (for example mistral/zai-glm-5-2 at coverage 0.5 in implement, missing tool_use 0.3 and repository_understanding 0.2) are auditable.
risks: Evidence base is three units only (deepswe population_size 28, tbench-v2.1 population_size 14, codereviewbench population_size 13); swebench-multilingual is scored but contributes no route evidence, and all three swebench-multimodal units are 'small-board-excluded'.

Half the plan is unevaluated: run_stage_plan, review_plan and general show coverage 0 for all nine routes, so the three baselines opencode-go/glm-5.3, openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol and openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna are unvalidated in those roles.

Every stage that does have eligible candidates has an unrankable baseline (implement baseline_coverage 0, review baseline_coverage 0.3, run_stage_break baseline_coverage 0), so no candidate rank is measured against the incumbent it would replace.

run_stage_break has a single eligible route; that winner's missing capability is adversarial_analysis at weight 0.4, the stage's largest weight, so its rank 1 rests on 0.6 coverage without its dominant capability observed.

review-stage ranks 2 through 4 sit at coverage 0.5 with software_engineering (0.3) and reasoning (0.2) unobserved, i.e. half the stage weight drives the ordering, and codereviewbench publishes uncertainty null so no interval bounds those percentiles.

The two gpt-5.6-luna routes share identical percentiles on both boards under the alias rule 'Published release is served by two providers; both routes claim this release', so the evidence cannot separate openai-codex from opencode-go even though their context limits differ (272000 vs 1050000).
contested_tolerance is documented as 'not yet applied to the gap between two routes in a stage', so apparent neighbour gaps inside a stage are unresolved by the scorecard's own admission.
disqualifiers: No routing change is supported for any of the six stages: three report 'no_comparable_evidence' and three report 'baseline_unrankable' with the rationale 'eligible candidates are listed without a baseline comparison'. Coverage is too low to decide, in every stage.

run_stage_break cannot be reassigned on this evidence: the only eligible candidate is missing the stage's 0.4-weight capability, and the incumbent opencode-go/hy3 has baseline_coverage 0, leaving the stage with no comparison at all.

general is disqualified from any judgement: all four weighted capabilities (instruction_following 0.3, reasoning 0.3, long_context 0.2, multimodal 0.2) are missing for every route, so the default route has zero measured weight.
divergence: The implement rank-1 tie group lists openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol (score 0.7745535714285714) and opencode-go/glm-5.3 (score 0.734375) as tied while their composites differ by less than contested_tolerance 0.05; I read the 'cost-broke-tie' selection of glm-5.3 as a price/context preference, not as evidence that it matches or exceeds sol on capability, especially given sol's output_price 30 versus glm-5.3's 4.4.

opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code takes review rank 1 from a single unit (codereviewbench, population_size 13, uncertainty null) while the deepswe population contains 'kimi-k2-7-code' at percentile 0.08928571428571429 that route_evidence does not claim under any alias_rule; the review leadership therefore rests on the narrowest base available and excludes a same-name agentic observation.

implement reports baseline_coverage 0 for opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash even though route_evidence holds a scored codereviewbench observation for it; that is a stage-definition artifact, and I would not read it as the model having no evidence, only none for this stage.

mistral/zai-glm-5-2 is scored in implement at coverage 0.5 from one deepswe observation whose percentile 0.16071428571428573 sits near the bottom of that 28-model board, so its rank 3 is an ordering among sparse rows rather than a demonstrated capability level.

review's baseline openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol is reported with coverage 0.3 and missing the stage's own highest-weight capability 'review' (0.5); the scorecard correctly withholds a comparison, but I diverge from any reading that treats the incumbent review route as confirmed adequate.

I do not treat the absence of evidence in run_stage_plan, review_plan and general as evidence of baseline adequacy or inadequacy; the scorecard's 'no rank' is a measurement gap, and the three incumbent routes should be logged as unevaluated rather than retained with confidence.
